result.topic_en: A transformation formula for the series sum 1/(e^{n^2 α}-1) under the condition αβ = 4π^3, its restatement for series whose coefficients count divisors that are perfect squares, and a note proposing the general series sum n^r/(e^{n^s x}-1).
result.transcription:
Add Ms a 94 18(74)
(74)
If $\alpha\beta = 4\pi^3$, then
$\frac{1}{e^{\alpha}-1} + \frac{1}{e^{4\alpha}-1} + \frac{1}{e^{9\alpha}-1} + \frac{1}{e^{16\alpha}-1} + \cdots$
$= \frac{\pi^2}{6\alpha} + \frac{1}{4} + \frac{\sqrt{\beta}}{4\pi}\left\{\zeta(\tfrac{1}{2}) + \sum_{n=1}^{n=\infty} \frac{\cos\sqrt{(n\beta)} - \sin\sqrt{(n\beta)} - e^{-\sqrt{(n\beta)}}}{\cosh\sqrt{(n\beta)} - \cos\sqrt{(n\beta)}}\right\}$.
In other words, if
[-$x^n$-] $\frac{x}{1-x} + \frac{x^4}{1-x^4} + \frac{x^9}{1-x^9} + \cdots = \sum \phi(n) x^n$
and $\frac{x}{1-x} + \frac{2x^4}{1-x^4} + \frac{3x^9}{1-x^9} + \cdots = \sum \psi(n) x^n$,
then
$\phi(1)e^{-\alpha} + \phi(2)e^{-2\alpha} + \phi(3)e^{-3\alpha} + \cdots$
$= \frac{\pi^2}{6\alpha} + \frac{\sqrt{\beta}}{2\pi}\left\{\tfrac{1}{2}\zeta(\tfrac{1}{2}) + \frac{\psi(1)}{\sqrt{1}} e^{-\sqrt{\beta}}(\cos\sqrt{\beta} - \sin\sqrt{\beta}) + \frac{\psi(2)}{\sqrt{2}} e^{-\sqrt{(2\beta)}}(\cos\sqrt{(2\beta)} - \sin\sqrt{(2\beta)})\right.$
$\left. + \frac{\psi(3)}{\sqrt{3}} e^{-\sqrt{(3\beta)}}(\cos\sqrt{(3\beta)} - \sin\sqrt{(3\beta)}) + \cdots\right\}$
with the condition $\alpha\beta = 4\pi^3$

$\frac{1^r}{e^{1^s x}-1} + \frac{2^r}{e^{2^s x}-1} + \frac{3^r}{e^{3^s x}-1} + \cdots$
where $s$ is a positive integer and $r-s$ is any even integer.

methods.what: Transformation formula for the series sum 1/(e^{n^2 α}-1) under the condition αβ = 4π^3, involving ζ(1/2) and a series of trigonometric and hyperbolic terms in √(nβ)
Definition of arithmetic functions φ(n) and ψ(n) as coefficients of Lambert-type series taken over square exponents
Equivalent restatement of the transformation as a series in φ(n)e^{-nα} expressed through ψ(n)/√n times e^{-√(nβ)}(cos√(nβ) − sin√(nβ))
General series sum n^r/(e^{n^s x}-1), with s a positive integer and r−s even

items.english: If αβ = 4π^3, then the sum of 1/(e^{n^2 α}-1) equals π^2/(6α) + 1/4 + (√β/(4π)) times {ζ(1/2) plus the stated series}.
In other words, the series sum φ(n)e^{-nα} equals π^2/(6α) + (√β/(2π)) times {½ζ(½) + sum of ψ(n)/√n · e^{-√(nβ)}(cos√(nβ) − sin√(nβ))}, with the condition αβ = 4π^3.
